newsitem.title: UK: Southern electric up on buy-back offer.
newsitem.headline: Southern electric up on buy-back offer.

text.p: Shares in Southern Electric led the electricity sector higher on Friday after the British regional electricity company said it would offer shareholders a buy-back scheme, worth around 156 million stg, traders said.
The stock was up 15p at 802-1/2 by 848 GMT.
"All the utilities are up on the back of this," one trader said. "Everyone's talking about buy-backs."
Southern plans to issue free bonus shares and then offer to buy the shares back for 60p each in two years time.
"This deal is all about saving on ACT (advanced corporation tax)," one analyst said.
By decreasing its reserve capital, Southern will avoid paying excess interest on ACT, which it can claim back from the British government in two years time.
Water companies will also be looking to decrease their reserve capital, the analyst said, as they do not have to pay ACT until 2005 and so have larger interest paymenst to avoid.
In the electricty sector, Yorkshire Electricity Plc, rose 5p to 816-1/2 and Scottish Hydro Plc, up 3p to 358-1/2p.
Thames Water also benefited, rising 10-1/2p to 669.
